chat.author: mblackmo
chat.text: She is a very good girl and wants her rightful place in the minutes!

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: Let's see how meetecho transcribe that

chat.author: Deb Cooley
chat.text: I don't think she actually managed to make the call.

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: yes that's the RFC for HTTP Message Signatures

chat.author: mblackmo
chat.text: I would be interested in participating (The Sequoia Project). Either structure would be fine with me.

chat.author: Omri Gazitt
chat.text: @dick are the slides available somewhere?

chat.author: Brian Campbell
chat.text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/slides-interim-2026-oauth-06-sessa-aauth-protocol-overview/

chat.author: Omri Gazitt
chat.text: Thanks Brian

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: Option C - Evolve OAuth to fill any gaps.

chat.author: Deb Cooley
chat.text: ^that

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: Like backporting GNAP's resource auth structure into RAR.

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: Option A and B both answer the question of what (this new aauth proposal) and where (new vs. existing wg)

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: yeah RAR is a good example of that precedent

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: Aaron's point is that the "what" is not the same question as "where"

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: I agree with Aaron.

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: While I'm flattered to be singled out -- there was a lot of public criticism of the Signature-Key header on the HTTP list.

chat.author: Brian Campbell
chat.text: i was also critical

chat.author: Atul Tulshibagwale
chat.text: Justin, thanks, do you have the link?

chat.author: Brian Campbell
chat.text: and so were a number of others

chat.author: Atul Tulshibagwale
chat.text: I guess those would need to be addressed before we make progress on AAuth, then?

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: @atul: this is the start of the thread about Signature-Key: https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/ietf-http-wg/2026JulSep/0163.html

chat.author: Atul Tulshibagwale
chat.text: thanks

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-rosenberg-oauth-aauth-01

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: Above is mine and Pat's early strawman for building ontop of OAuth

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: "let's not do it" would be option D

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: OIDC was built on OAuth 2.0 though

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: Analogy can cut both ways

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: Jeff's point stands.

chat.author: Deb Cooley
chat.text: OIDC did not deprecate SAML.  Leaving us with all sorts of issues wrt crypt migration.

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: OIDC could not have deprecated a spec in another SDO.

chat.author: Deb Cooley
chat.text: true, but migration from one to the other didn't happen.

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: yet

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: It has in a lot of places, just not universally by any stretch

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: the law of the world has it that the stronger you want to deprecate something, the longer it outlives

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: we've been trying to kill SIP2.0 forever and have failed.

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: :face_with_peeking_eye:

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: high cardinality, bilateral protocols, are very hard to upgrade

chat.author: Deb Cooley
chat.text: same for PKCS1 v1.5

chat.author: Deb Cooley
chat.text: which isn't a protocol it is merely a format

chat.author: Atul Tulshibagwale
chat.text: Dick should be pushing to deprecate AAuth then :D

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: Old standards don't die, they fade away... slowly

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: The other benefot of OAuth evolution is there is no OAuth sunset program in the future... (maybe some features of OAuth is sunset, but not the full protocol)

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: Said otherwise, while an AS in 2028 might look less than an AS in 2026, those AS are already deployed at many places and can be upgraded. Person Servers and Access Servers?

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: Evolution has migration built in

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: the main question is: what problem do we want to solve.

chat.author: Brian Campbell
chat.text: it is difficult

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: as opposed to: what parts of Dick's protocol do we want

chat.author: Brian Campbell
chat.text: can confirm

chat.author: Deb Cooley
chat.text: is that the last interim?

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: Right, and everything that comes into the WG would need to be able to change independently of the original proposal.

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: @deb there is no next week but one more the week after

chat.author: Deb Cooley
chat.text: yes, agree

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: we already have a way to do not-preregistered clients now with CIMD

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: as yet another example

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: right

chat.author: Dick Hardt
chat.text: it is not an instance of a client Aaron

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: and also pushed reqs if we wanted

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: and client attestation
